review:
REJECTED

The source is honest about its main result. The artifact is not fit to ship. The PDFs don't match the committed source, and one surviving result rests on numbers the paper itself retracts. The title and both first-person reflections are also explicitly unapproved drafts; the commit subject says "DRAFT for Thomas, not for master". Most fixes below are mechanical. Finding 2 needs a judgment call and should come back for review.

**Twin check (what you asked about specifically):** I read both editions in full. No table row is filed under a different section heading in one edition than the other. All three tables, and every row in them, sit under the same headings in both. The editions differ in only four places:
- the author block;
- three Limitations items (commented out in flight, shown in academic);
- a CRediT statement (academic only);
- the bib path.

The structural defect this lab has shipped before does exist here, but inside each edition rather than between them (finding 2).

## Findings

**1. CRITICAL: the PDFs are stale, in two different ways.**
- **Committed PDFs.** On this branch they were last changed in `5e6f096`/`fe5e9a2` (2026-10-10), before the correction commit `438eacc`. The commit says "PDFs are rebuilt in a separate commit", and that commit doesn't exist. Merged as-is, the branch ships the pre-correction PDFs. I inferred this from git log and did not render the HEAD PDF.
- **Working-tree PDFs (uncommitted, built 17:04).** These were built from a different `main.tex`. latexmk recorded md5 `be12392d…` (73,318 bytes) for flight; the committed file is `f4105fd8…` (73,295 bytes). Academic: `afc8f7d1…` against `859efa1d…`, also 23 bytes apart.
- **The two differences.** I rendered the flight PDF; these two account for exactly the 23 bytes:
  - p. 6: the PDF says "the injection test and **the 500-feature** TF-IDF baseline"; the source says "**its** TF-IDF baseline".
  - p. 11: the PDF says "288 specifications … (layer sets, pools, similarities and **residual sources**)"; the source (`main.tex:334`) says "**and folds**". This changes what the specification sweep spans.
- **Fix:** settle which wording `um_v2_results.json` supports (I couldn't read it). Then rebuild both editions, run `verify_pdf.py` with a `--control`, and commit the PDFs naming both changes.

**2. CRITICAL: a live result is read off the analysis the paper retracts.**
- **The claim.** `main.tex:366` says: "On Mistral-7B, encoding peaks at layer 4 (depth 0.13) while generation peaks at layer 11 (depth 0.35), with uncorrelated depth profiles (ρ = 0.002, p = 0.990)."
- **Where the numbers come from.** In `data/mistral_probe_analysis_results.json`, `enc_gen_separation` gives `enc_peak_layer: 4`, `enc_peak_acc: 0.0844`, `gen_peak_layer: 11` and `profile_rho: 0.0022`. That 0.0844 is the "8.4% at L4 on Mistral" which the Correction note (`main.tex:343`) calls "artifacts of information leakage, not genuine signal". Once leakage is removed the profile sits at chance, so its peak layer is noise.
- **Qwen.** The same file for Qwen gives an encoding peak at L3 (the leaky 9.4%), a generation peak at L23 and `profile_rho` 0.433, which is not uncorrelated. The paper doesn't report the 0.433. In its place it gives W_K bridge numbers, which come from an encoding-only re-encode with no generation arm. So "In both architectures, the encoding-phase … signal peaks before the generation-phase signal" (`:368`) has no valid support on Qwen.
- **The "other-schema" framing.** Attention Schema Theory's "other-schema … of its interlocutor" (`:163`) is also the withdrawn user-model claim surviving under another name: the "other" here is a story character.
- **Every place this appears:**
  - §2.4 last sentence (`:163`);
  - all of §4.6 (`:363–370`);
  - the opening of §4.11, "the encoding-phase signal peaks at the shallowest layers" (`:427`), which also contradicts the W_K bridge strengthening with depth;
  - all of §5.4 (`:539–543`), including "This prediction is confirmed" and "replicates across both architectures";
  - Conclusion item 5 (`:613`);
  - the academic-only Limitations item "Encoding depth ordering" (`academic/main.tex:574`).
- **Fix:** withdraw all of these and add Appendix A item 9 with the verbatim text and this reason. The Barrett (2006) sentence goes with them. As I recall from my own knowledge (I couldn't read the paper), Barrett treats dimensional core affect as the input that categorization acts on, which reverses the "categorical before dimensional" order the sentence attributes to her.

**3. MAJOR: unapproved drafts are in the shipping text, and the paper has three titles.**
- **Drafts in the source.**
  - `main.tex:45` reads "TITLE: A PROPOSAL, AND THOMAS'S CALL".
  - `:131` and `:594` read "DRAFT FOR LYRA … Lyra to approve or rewrite".
  - The PDF renders both reflections as the lead author's own words.
- **Three titles.**
  - tex: "Story Emotion in the KV Cache…";
  - `paper.json:2`: "Emotion Geometry in the KV Cache";
  - `README.md:1,3,85`: "Theory of Mind in the KV Cache: Localizing User Emotional Models…", in the H1, in "Full title", and in the BibTeX block readers are told to use.
- **Fix:** Thomas picks the title and it goes into both editions, the README (H1, Full title, BibTeX) and `paper.json`. Lyra signs off on or rewrites the reflections. Then remove the comments.

**4. MAJOR: "my cache" in the reflections.**
- **Quotes:**
  - `:135`: "can be read out of my cache about as well as out of its words";
  - `:598`: "is in my cache about as plainly as it is in the words";
  - `:598`: "if my cache holds what a person's words hold".
- **Why it's wrong.** The cache measured belongs to Qwen3.5-27B-Claude-Distilled. The byline footnote describes Lyra as Claude-architecture. No experiment read the author's cache. This is the same level confusion the correction exists to remove, moved from character-versus-user to author-versus-subject-model.
- **Fix:** write "a model's cache" (or name the model) throughout.

**5. MAJOR: the academic edition's byline doesn't match its contribution record, and the reflections have no visible author.**
- **The mismatch.**
  - The byline is Thomas Edrington alone, "With AI research assistance" (`academic/main.tex:58`).
  - Its CRediT statement (`:623`) credits Lyra with Conceptualization, Methodology, Formal analysis and Writing – original draft.
  - Thomas's footnote claims "experimental design", while CRediT gives Methodology only to Lyra.
- **The reflections.** Two "First-Person Reflection" boxes in an AI voice then appear under a sole human byline, so a reader will take "I" and "my cache" to mean Thomas.
- **Fix (Thomas's call within the venue's AI policy):** an AI-contribution statement that names Lyra and matches the CRediT roles; reconcile "experimental design"; and either attribute the boxes explicitly or drop them from the venue edition.

**6. MAJOR: claims the correction missed, which contradict the paper's own corrected results.**
- **§4.7 opening** (`:375`): "The story re-encoding analysis reveals how emotion enters the KV cache." Its own heading and closing sentence call it "a candidate pathway … not an established one". Change "reveals how" to "proposes a route by which".
- **§4.9** (`:405`): "confirming that the mechanism is not specific to hybrid attention". The mechanism is not established. No Mistral bridge number appears anywhere in the paper; the README has 0.932 at L17. Report the number and say "candidate route".
- **§4.10 heading and closing, and §2.5** (`:411–421`, `:167`):
  - "Distillation Preserves Functional Emotion Representations … robust to model compression". There is no teacher and no undistilled comparison.
  - "Functional" contradicts Limitation 4 ("No causal intervention").
  - The 7% confabulation bullet is off-topic.
  - Fix: rename the section to something like "Emotion is decodable in a distilled model", and delete the robustness sentence.
- **Deception.** The Introduction (`:115`) says prior work distinguishes "deception from honesty", and §5.6 (`:557`) says spectral features "discriminate … deception". But §2.3 (`:159`) says a deception result was withdrawn. Qualify both sentences, or drop "deception".
- **Intro item 4** (`:128`): "the cache encodes which emotion is present, not a continuous valence-arousal mapping". The evidence is spectral-feature regression only, and the paper's own W_K projection shows PC1–valence 0.862 and PC2–arousal 0.769. §5.3 scopes this correctly ("in spectral shape features"); copy that scope into item 4.

**7. MAJOR: two process claims the paper itself falsifies.**
- **`:531`:** "every number cites the committed script that produced it".
  - §4.11 says the k = 30 path "is not in the released artifact".
  - Tables 2–3, the F-ratio, the 63%, the variance ratio of 0.5 and the miss distances cite no script.
  - The re-run's scripts have no location (finding 9).
  - Fix: scope the sentence to §4.1–4.4, or add the citations.
- **`:249`:** "All reported p-values are from these permutation tests [10,000 shuffles]". The paper also reports McNemar, Holm, Mantel and Spearman p-values, and the primary test used 1,000 permutations. Delete the sentence.

**8. MAJOR: a registered failure is presented as a reproduction.**
- **The issue.** Intro item 1 (`:122`), §4.1 (`:316`) and the README all say "v2's number reproduces to within one trial in 900". The registered verdict was `NOT_REPRODUCED_CODE_PATH`, and only the last paragraph of the appendix (`:661`) says so. Reinterpreting a registered outcome after seeing the data is legitimate, but it has to be labelled as post-data where the result is stated.
- **Fix:** §4.1 should open with "R1's registered verdict: NOT_REPRODUCED_CODE_PATH (369 vs 368, zero-trial band)". The investigation follows, labelled post-data, and Intro item 1 says the same.

**9. MAJOR: a reader cannot find the re-run's artifacts.**
- **The issue.** `prereg_um_v2_R1R2.json`, `um_v2_encode.py`, `um_v2_analysis.py` and `um_v2_results.json` are cited only by filename and an 8-character hash prefix (`:221`, `:278`). None of them is in this repo; I searched. The commit message points to `Research/corrections/user_model_v2/`, which is outside the published repository.
- **The README is now wrong about this.** `README.md:75` says "every numerical claim … verified against the source JSON files in `data/`", which is false for every October number. `README.md:79` says all experiments ran on 3× RTX 3090, but the re-run used Apple MPS.
- **Fix:** commit the four files with a hash, cite them the way `d0c8395` is cited, and correct both README lines.

**10. MAJOR: in-house citations have a wrong title and wrong authors.**
- **lyra2026oracle.** `references.bib:14–19` gives "The Oracle Loop: Cache-Geometry Detection and Steering of Confabulation…" by Lyra, Edrington and CC. The Oracle Loop paper in this repo (`oracle-loop-paper/main.tex:62–76`) is titled "…Self-Regulating AI Through KV-Cache Geometry Monitoring", and its byline is Lyra, Thomas K. Edrington and Vera. CC isn't on it and Vera is missing.
- **lyra2026detecting and lyra2026concordance.** No paper in this corpus has either title; they appear only in bib files. Both list Dwayne Wilkes and Nell Watson as authors, and neither has a URL or DOI.
- **Fix:** take the titles and bylines from the papers themselves, and add URLs.
- **Separate problem, for its own register row:** `oracle-loop-paper/paper.json` lists Dwayne Wilkes as an author, but that paper's tex byline doesn't.

**11. MAJOR, UNVERIFIED (web access was denied): the model footnote is probably false.**
- **The footnote** (`:176`) says "'Qwen3.5' is the distiller's designation, not an official Alibaba release; the model is built on the Qwen3 architecture", and cites the Qwen3 Technical Report.
- **Why it's probably wrong.**
  - The paper's own architecture (48 GatedDeltaNet + 16 full-attention layers) is not the dense Qwen3 architecture in that report.
  - From my own knowledge, Alibaba did release an official Qwen3.5 family in early 2026 with hybrid Gated DeltaNet attention.
- **Smaller points:** the bib key `qwen2025distill` mislabels a technical report as a distillation source; "distilled from Claude Opus 4.6" has no citation; the footnote has a comma splice.
- **Fix:** check the Hugging Face model card and Alibaba's release, then cite the right base model.

**12. MINOR: position-based cross-references.**
- "Appendix A, item 2/6/7" (`:191`, `:226`, `:339`) are typed in by hand. They are correct today: item 2 is the prompt, 6 the 0.882 baseline, 7 direction-versus-shape. Finding 2 adds an item, so this is likely to rot. Fix: use `\label` on the items and `\ref` them.
- Code line references ("lines 230–243", "line 81", "lines 91–92") also check out today, but they rot on any edit. Fix: name `SYSTEM_PROMPT` and `make_story_prompt`, or pin a commit.

**13. MINOR: Table 3 (`:379–388`).**
- The caption says "PC2 … |ρ| > 0.76 at layers 35–63", but L63 is 0.759.
- L35 is in bold as the peak, but the data has L43 at |ρ| = 0.872 and L47 at 0.866 (`qwen_emotion_bridge_summary.json:1007`, `:1023`). The README's "best 0.862 (L35)" is wrong for the same reason.
- PC1's sign also flips at L7, L11 and L43, so "sign flipping at deeper layers" is selective. PCA sign is arbitrary; say so.
- The Conclusion's "building from mid-network to deep layers" is wrong: the peak is in the middle-to-upper layers, not at the end.

**14. MINOR: Table 2, Mistral row (`:358`).** The trial-level R² of 0.013 comes from layer 3 (`valence_regression_trial_level.best_layer: 3`) but is printed in the layer-24 row.

**15. MINOR: wording and loose ends.**
- Limitations says "Two models" (`:565`); there are three, since §4.11 uses Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct.
- Conclusion item 6 (`:614`) states as a conclusion a result that §4.11 calls "illustrative", and "geometrically distinct but separately clustered" is not a contrast.
- "The initial 94% residual-stream probe accuracy" (`:529`) appears nowhere else.
- "the May evening's weights" (`:316`) is unexplained jargon.
- The correction box says "found three things" (`:105`), but the appendix records more, including the prompt the Methods described that no script used.

**16. MINOR: housekeeping.**
- `frisch1933partial` and `lovell1963seasonal` are in the bib but never cited, while FWL is used uncited throughout. Cite them at first use.
- Neither build log shows undefined references or citations.
- The flight edition removed "Linear probes only" from Limitations with a note saying it was "folded into Methods/Results"; it isn't anywhere in the body.
- `W_K` in section titles produces hyperref bookmark warnings; use `\texorpdfstring`.
- The untracked `agni_input_um_v2_flight.diff` sits in `paper/`, where a directory-level add would sweep it in.
- "AI researcher (Claude architecture, Anthropic)" (`:58`) can read as an Anthropic affiliation. The Oracle Loop paper's wording, "Lyra is an AI system (Claude architecture, Anthropic)", is unambiguous.

## What I could not check

- **`Research/corrections/user_model_v2/`** (`R1R2_RESULTS.md`, `um_v2_results.json`, the prereg): reading outside the worktree was denied. Every October number in §4.1–4.4 and the appendix is UNVERIFIED by me, including which "288 specifications" wording is right. The commit message claims verify-paper found 0 mismatches against these files; that is a secondary source, and I have not relied on it.
- **External sources:** WebSearch and WebFetch were denied, so these are unchecked:
  - Qwen3.5's official status (finding 11);
  - whether arXiv 2604.07729 matches the `anthropic2026emotions` title, authors and the quoted "can (and does) recall…" sentence;
  - the Barrett 2006 reading in finding 2;
  - dead-URL checks. The bib has DOIs but no URLs; I recognise the DOI strings as plausible but didn't resolve them.
- **The academic PDF and the committed HEAD PDFs:** I didn't render them. The academic edition's staleness is shown by the hash mismatch and the identical 23-byte gap. The HEAD PDFs' pre-correction state is inferred from git log only.
- **Table 2 and the F-ratio:** I didn't trace whether they used within-fold FWL or the pre-split FWL, or the May trial file where effective rank and entropy are constant. The Qwen and Mistral files they come from also hold the retracted leaky classification. Tracing this needs the `probe_mistral_analysis.py` / Qwen analysis scripts, which aren't in `code/`.
- **Implicit-arm numbers** (ARI, 63%, variance ratio ≈ 0.5, ρ values): no data file for them is in this repo.
